title: CME’s share of XRP futures jumps as token rallies 40% in a week
summary: Title: XRP rallies 40% as futures traders cut leverage and CME exposure grows URL Source: https://www.coindesk.com/markets/2026/09/01/xrp-futures-are-shifting-toward-cme-as-institutional-participation-grows Published Time: 2026-09-01T03:49:39.592Z Markdown Content: Updated 2 hrs ago Published 2 hrs ago 2 min read ![Image 1: CME Group Headquarters (CoinDesk Archives)](https://www.coindesk.com/_next/image?url=https%3A%2F%2Fcdn.sanity.io%2Fimages%2Fs3y3vcno%2Fproduction%2Fb119fde813835a73b12fcb4cb0e3a811abe61149-1500x1021.jpg%3Frect%3D0%2C89%2C1500%2C844%26w%3D1920%26h%3D1080%26auto%3Dformat&w=3840&q=75) CME Group Headquarters (CoinDesk Archives) Summary * Total XRP futures open interest fell 16% from Aug. 17 to Aug. 31 even as XRP’s price rose nearly 40%, signaling that traders were reducing leverage during the rally. * Open interest on CME increased about 36%, lifting the regulated exchange’s share of outstanding XRP futures exposure to roughly 17% from 10%. * Leveraged funds more than doubled their net-short position to the equivalent of about 116 million XRP, though the contracts may hedge holdings elsewhere rather than represent outright bearish bets. A growing share of XRP futures trading is moving toward CME even as traders cut leveraged positions across crypto exchanges. Total XRP open interest, or the amount tied up in outstanding futures contracts, fell to about 2.34 billion tokens on Aug. 31 from 2.77 billion on Aug. 17, [CoinGlass data](https://www.coinglass.com/open-interest/XRP) show. XRP moved the other way, climbing from roughly $0.99 to $1.38 over the same period. CME, the regulated U.S. futures exchange used heavily by professional trading firms and investment managers, bucked that decline. XRP open interest there rose to about 387 million tokens from 284 million, an [increase of roughly 36%](https://www.cftc.gov/dea/options/financial_lof.htm?source=content_type%3Areact%7Cfirst_level_url%3Aarticle%7Csection%3Amain_content%7Cbutton%3Ab

(Getty Images) Summary * Wallets linked to North Korea’s state-sponsored hacking squad, the Lazarus Group, have sold more than $30 million in bitcoin on Hyperliquid in recent weeks, blockchain data from Arkham shows. * Hackers’ use of the platform comes as U.S. President Donald Trump’s administration explores ways to bring Hyperliquid into the regulated U.S. market. North Korean hackers are moving funds through Hyperliquid, selling more than $30 million in bitcoin [BTC$79,166.61](https://www.coindesk.com/price/bitcoin) on the decentralized derivatives trading platform in the past three weeks alone, according to blockchain data. The data, which was reviewed exclusively by blockchain analytics firm Arkham at CoinDesk's request, identified wallets linked to North Korea’s state-sponsored hacking squad, the Lazarus Group, actively moving funds through the platform. Proceeds from the hackers’ recent bitcoin sales were used to acquire ether [ETH$2,483.91](https://www.coindesk.com/price/ethereum) and solana (SOL), which were subsequently transferred to other crypto exchanges, including Kraken, LBank and KuCoin.
